label: The canon drift is three-way and asymmetric: option C carries the series-parent case only in AGENTS.md section 2 and quick-reference section 8, while quick-reference section 9 and both runtime constants omit it; option B carries the new/unrelated gate in AGENTS.md and quick-reference section 9 but the runtime question reads as a neutral create-new. The runtime comment calls its own text the menu a human answers, so the surface with the least grouping language is the one the operator sees.

The runtime menu cannot carry dynamic sibling evidence: GATE_3_QUESTION and GATE_3_MUTATION_NOTICE are frozen string arrays and gate3QuestionHash hashes the question content through the canonical policy block with GATE_SPEC_FOLDER_QUESTION_ID; with the frozen baseline and byte-length receipt tests, a wording change must be one coordinated set (constants plus regenerated baseline and pinned hash fixtures) and per-decision evidence must come from a separate surface. The deny path relays the same mutation notice, so fixing the option C sentence there also fixes what a blocked model relays.

The plan surface already has the routing capability but no proposal step: plan.md is a thin router whose presentation wording lives in speckit-plan-presentation.txt and behavior in speckit-plan.yaml, so grouping UX belongs in those assets; --phase-folder, :with-phases and the relationship flags already provide mechanical routes, but relationship flags only record links and are gated on --record-relationships=yes, and :auto resolves setup through a pre-bound answers block rather than an auto-selection.

Grouping by default must mean recommendation ordering plus evidence because the guardrails already exist: quick-reference section 9 orders C first for a distinct related workstream including a series parent and states the agent recommends but never selects autonomously; AGENTS.md fixes the four stable labels and makes B conditional on new or unrelated work. Pre-selection, pre-binding or blocking on grouping would violate existing rules; the compliant levers are wording, recommendation order, evidence presentation and a required justification for B.

create.sh holds the only creation-time series-parent wording but fires after the menu decision and its evidence is not yet trustworthy: the lister writes to stderr inside scaffold on the resolve_branch_name paths, its candidates are top-level only, the new work's topic never reaches it, and zero-match or missing-metadata paths are silent. The iteration-2 shortlist items 3, 4 and 6 widen the candidate set, pass and rank the topic with an explicit no-close-matches line, and expose recent_packets in the --json payload; items 1, 2, 5 and 7 are the trust pre-conditions and item 8 keeps the mechanism advisory-only and non-blocking.

Grouping-default UX is recommendation-only: labels A/B/C/D stay stable and the agent never selects autonomously; B requires a new/unrelated justification; every advisory surface (Gate 3 dialog and deny relay, plan intake, create.sh lister) must never block, auto-route or pre-select.

direction: Inlining dynamic sibling evidence (ranked recent-packet rows) into GATE_3_QUESTION or GATE_3_MUTATION_NOTICE
reason: The constants are static string arrays and the question content is hashed through the canonical policy block with byte-pinned fixtures (f-iter001-006, f-iter003-002); per-decision evidence must come from a separate pre-decision surface.

direction: Pre-selecting or auto-routing option C in the Gate 3 dialog or the plan intake for auto/unattended runs
reason: Violates the existing AI Agent Rule (recommend, never select autonomously) and the stable-labels contract; unattended runs must use the pre-bound setup answers block instead.
